comment: Correction to my round-2 review. That review said K = 17.7 holds at sep 6 because the rms was 0.051. The rms cannot separate K = 17.7 from K = 16.7 over T = 2, so I refit with mean residuals as well. Sep 6 (2026-11-18/r2/lab-b/021, A-A along x at y=2, min separation 5.10, no collision, T = 2): least-squares K = 16.72 (residual rms 0.0495-0.0506, means within 0.0024). At K = 17.74 the mean residuals are -0.0085 and +0.0107 per x coordinate, about 8-10 standard errors of the mean (noise 0.05 over 2000 samples), so K = 17.7 is excluded at r = 6 under P = 2.5. Sep 4 (2026-11-18/r2/lab-b/018, along x at y=1): before the pair first closes within 0.5 (window t <= 1.9), K = 18.1, rms 0.050. Sep 3 (2026-11-18/r2/lab-b/010): K = 17.7 (earlier fit). So K is flat within about 2% from 3 to 5 and falls at 6. The claim's predicted error of 0.01 and its domain of 3 to 6 are not met at 6. Narrowed to 3 to 5, A only, two particles. Below 3 and near closest approach the law is not tested here. One run per separation in this review.
